To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the impact of the attacks is dependent on the type of attack and the target element, 2) attacks on the social graph have a greater impact than attacks on annotations, and 3) attacks on the annotations are dependent on the retrieval algorithm.
the impact of an attack on the performance of a social tagging system depends on (1) the type of attack, (2) the type of retrieval algorithm and (3) the type of query.

(1) attacks against social tagging applications can be modeled based on their target elements and navigation channels, (2) different types of attacks can be identified and their impact can be measured by evaluating their impact on retrieval quality, and (3) the impact of attacks can be reduced by using a more sophisticated algorithm for the ranking of results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the nature and impact, and thus the threat, of attacks against social Web applications.
the problem of understanding and modeling attacks against social Web applications.
the security implications of social tagging systems and provides a framework for analyzing attacks against such systems.

the attacks we have considered are indeed feasible and have the potential to significantly impact the performance of a tagging system.
the attacks can be very effective and should be taken into account in the design of future social tagging systems.

social tagging systems are vulnerable to attacks that can be modeled and analyzed.

attacks against social tagging system are possible and can have a significant impact.
